rm .env.local && cat > README.md <<'EOF'
# Notely

A small team notes app. Next.js App Router + TypeScript + Tailwind.

## Status

- Users live in `src/lib/users.ts` as an in-memory list.
- Authentication is WorkOS AuthKit: email + password and Google sign-in on hosted pages.
- `/dashboard` requires a signed-in user and shows them plus the team.
- There is no billing and no email yet.

## Auth setup

1. Create an app at https://dashboard.workos.com.
2. Under **Authentication**, turn on **Email + Password** and **Google OAuth**
   (WorkOS's demo Google credentials work in staging; add your own for production).
3. Under **Redirects**, set:
   - Redirect URI: `http://localhost:3000/auth/callback`
   - Sign-in endpoint (initiate login URI): `http://localhost:3000/sign-in`
   - Sign-out redirect: `http://localhost:3000/`
4. `cp .env.example .env.local` and fill in the real values.

How it fits together:

- `src/proxy.ts`: AuthKit proxy. Refreshes sessions and sends signed-out visitors on
  `/dashboard/*` to sign-in. `/` is public.
- `/sign-in`, `/sign-up`: redirect to the hosted AuthKit screens.
- `/auth/callback`: finishes sign-in, links the WorkOS user to a Notely user, then goes to `/dashboard`.
- `src/lib/users.ts`: `getCurrentUser()` / `requireCurrentUser()` read the session and
  match the WorkOS user to a Notely user by WorkOS id, then by email, or create one.

## Develop

```bash
npm run dev
```
EOF
git status --short

content.text:
Notely now has sign-in through **WorkOS AuthKit**: email + password sign-up and sign-in, Google sign-in, and `/dashboard` is closed to signed-out visitors. It builds and lints cleanly, but I haven't done a real sign-in, because that needs real WorkOS credentials.

**Why WorkOS:** Notely has no database yet; users are an in-memory list. A hosted service handles passwords, Google sign-in and sessions without adding a database, and AuthKit is free up to 1M monthly users. The repo already had a WorkOS guide (`docs/workos.md`). Its last section reads like marketing, so I checked its code against the installed package (v4.6.2) rather than taking it on trust. It matches and supports Next 16.

**What changed:**
- **`src/lib/users.ts`**:
  - `getCurrentUser()` now reads the real session instead of returning the first user.
  - New `requireCurrentUser()` sends visitors to sign-in.
  - New `upsertUserFromAuth()` links a WorkOS login to a Notely user. It matches by WorkOS id, then by email, so Ada and Grace keep their records when they sign in. Otherwise it creates a new user.
- **`src/proxy.ts`**: blocks signed-out visitors from `/dashboard/*` and keeps sessions fresh. `/` stays public. The dashboard page also checks the user itself, so it's protected twice.
- **New routes**:
  - `/sign-in` and `/sign-up` redirect to the WorkOS sign-in and sign-up pages.
  - `/auth/callback` completes sign-in, links the user, and goes to `/dashboard`.
  - Sign-out is a server action in `src/app/actions/auth.ts`.
- **Pages**: the home page now shows Sign in / Sign up, or a dashboard link and Sign out if you're signed in. The dashboard has a Sign out button. I replaced the Create Next App home page and page title.
- **`.env.example`** has the four placeholder variables. I added `!.env.example` to `.gitignore`, because the existing `.env*` rule would have kept the file out of git.
- **`README.md`** now has the setup steps.

**What I tested:** with the placeholder keys, `/` returns 200 and shows the sign-in buttons. `/dashboard` while signed out redirects to WorkOS sign-in. `/sign-in` and `/sign-up` send you to the right WorkOS screen. The full round trip back through `/auth/callback` is untested.

**To make it work for real:**
1. In the WorkOS dashboard, turn on Email + Password and Google.
2. Set the redirect URI, sign-in URL and sign-out redirect listed in the README. Sign out won't work until the sign-out redirect is set.
3. Copy `.env.example` to `.env.local` and fill in the real values.

**Worth knowing:**
- Users are still in memory, so anyone who signs up disappears when the server restarts. That's the next thing to fix: `upsertUserFromAuth` is where a database would plug in.
- `npx tsc --noEmit` on a fresh checkout reports an error that `LayoutProps` can't be found. That's in the existing layout file and goes away once `next build` or `next dev` generates its types.

Nothing is committed.
